title: Java Script (No, Not That One): Modern Automation with Java
summary: The talk shows how modern Java has become practical for scripting and automation, thanks to shebang support, single-file execution, and instance main methods. It also covers JBang for dependency management and advanced use cases, with live demos demonstrating fast, maintainable Java scripts.

speakers.name: Loïc Magnette
speakers.bio: Loïc Magnette is a seasoned software developer with a strong background in consulting. Currently a senior developer at Oniryx, he specializes in Java and Angular, delivering innovative solutions and sharing his knowledge as a speaker. As a co-organizer of the Belgian Java User Group (BeJUG), he fosters connections within the developer community. Outside of tech, Loïc’s passion for wildlife inspires his work and creativity.

title: The Importance of HITL to Avoid Chaos and EU Regulations for AI
summary: The talk explains Human-in-the-Loop design for AI coding agents in enterprise workflows, covering approval gates, audit trails, compliance with the EU AI Act, and failure risks in microservices. It offers practical patterns for adding human checkpoints to CI/CD without sacrificing speed or control.

speakers.name: Juan Antonio Breña 🇪🇸🇪🇺
speakers.bio: From programming microservices to leading engineering teams: this is how I've spent my last 20 years in technology as a Java/Spring ecosystem specialist. My career has evolved from designing cloud-native architectures and migrating legacy systems to leading engineering teams focused on high-quality results and efficient processes.

title: Quarkus Community BOF
summary: Quarkus is a fast-growing Java framework with 800+ extensions and 1,000+ contributors, now under the CommonHaus Foundation. Meet core team and contributors at Devoxx to discuss the ecosystem, share ideas, and ask anything—especially about Quarkus, community involvement, and its work on Agentic AI.

speakers.name: Dimitris Andreadis
speakers.bio:
Dimitris is an open source veteran with 25+ years of experience in IT and he is currently a (Red Hat) Sr.Director of Engineering at IBM in charge of the Cloud Native Runtimes group that includes Quarkus, Vert.x, SpringBoot and Node.js. He also served as the JBoss AS project lead and he has been a JBoss addict and contributor from the early start-up days. He worked previously at Intracom and Motorola in the areas of NMS/OSS, designing reusable frameworks and distributed systems. Dimitris studied computer science at the Technological Educational Institute of Athens and received an M.Sc. by research from University College Dublin, Ireland.

Dimitris is a passionate advocator of Opensource & Red Hat technologies and has presented on a variety of events and conferences around the world. He has been an invited speaker at various Java/Linux community events and user groups, and he has delivered inspirational talks on technology and Open Source in universities and educational institutes. In his spare time he has also helped with the organization of technology enablement events for children, like Scratch Days, Devoxx4Kids and JCrete4Kids.

title: Who will build software after AI?
summary: An open discussion on how AI-assisted development affects children’s coding education, including whether kids should still learn to code, which skills matter most, and how to make technology engaging and accessible. The session explores the future of Devoxx4Kids, robotics, and nurturing the next generation of makers.

speakers.name: Eddy Vos
speakers.bio:
Eddy is the chairman of Devoxx4Kids Netherlands and an Engineering Manager at Ahold Delhaize Netherlands. He has a focus on AI, Data, FinOps and Java.
He loves to share his knowledge and help in his free time, with the Devoxx4Kids Foundation, kids to learn how to code in a fun way.

title: Welcome to Devoxx
summary: The welcome opening keynote for Devoxx Belgium 2026 by the founder of Devoxx giving a general update on the conference.

speakers.name: Stephan Janssen
speakers.bio: With three decades of experience in the Java ecosystem and as the founder of Devoxx, one of the world's most prestigious developer conferences, Stephan brings unparalleled expertise in developer tools and workflows. His AI journey began 7+ years ago with CNNs for basketball analysis, evolving into 5 years of intensive work with GPT models. As the creator of DevoxxGenie, he's been at the forefront of AI-assisted development, building real-world applications and helping thousands of developers level up their skills.

title: From Brainless to Brilliant — Giving an Open-Source Robot a Mind of Its Own
summary: A hobbyist built AURA, a personal “brain” for an open robot platform, using only a laptop. It recognizes household members, keeps learned and told information separate, and seeks permission before committing code. The project demonstrates how accessible robotics and AI now are.

speakers.name: Jan Van Wassenhove
speakers.bio:
Jan Van Wassenhove is the Technical Director of the System Integrations Business Line for the BeLux region at Sopra Steria, where he drives technology solutions and services, supported by his team of architects. With a strong background in Java development, Jan has evolved into an experienced architect and project manager, with in-depth expertise in Agile methodologies.

Remarkably, he is also the initiator of “SCRUM”, a new programming language he conceived. This creation perfectly reflects his innovative mindset and constant drive to explore new technological territories — and proves, with a wink, that everyone really can become a SCRUM master… in code.

Throughout his career, he has contributed to numerous projects in both the public and private sectors, with a particular focus on banking and public administrations.

title: Half of a billion Idle GPUs: The Case for On-Device AI
summary: This keynote argues that Apple Silicon devices form a massive, underused AI compute fleet. Drawing on the MLX ecosystem, it shows how on-device inference can handle frontier models through advanced optimization, and why privacy, latency, cost, and sovereignty will shift more AI workloads from cloud to device.

speakers.name: Prince Canuma
speakers.bio: Prince Canuma is Founder and CEO of Neywa Labs, building the inference stack for Apple Silicon. He is the creator and primary maintainer of the MLX open-source ecosystem — mlx-vlm, mlx-audio, and mlx-embeddings — with over 4M combined downloads, foundational to on-device AI on Apple hardware. He previously led developer experience at Neptune AI and worked at Arcee on post-training and inference optimization. His work focuses on model optimization and making AI accessible on local hardware.

title: A Fleet of AI Agents, Each in Its Own Sandbox: Inside Docker's Agentic Platform
summary: Docker’s Agentic Platform enables AI agents to autonomously read issues, code, test, and prepare pull requests in isolated sandboxes with secure identities. The talk covers orchestrated specialist agents, parallel workflows, and key production lessons on cost, hallucinations, human oversight, safety, and observability.

speakers.name: Jean-Laurent de Morlhon
speakers.bio:
Jean-Laurent de Morlhon is SVP, GenAI Acceleration at Docker, where he focuses on making AI application and agent development simpler for developers.
Over more than nine years at Docker, he has held several engineering leadership roles, helping build and scale teams working on developer tools and infrastructure.
Today, his work focuses on GenAI developer experience, from running models locally to MCP, sandboxes and agentic workflows, with a particular interest in making emerging AI technologies practical, reliable and easy for developers to use.

title: The Year of the Runtime
summary: AI coding agents reduce the importance of language syntax, making runtime performance and operability more critical. Java’s JVM and standard library are a strong fit: newer JDKs continually improve speed, observability, garbage collection, and usability without changing the programming model, with major innovations underway in Valhalla, Leyden, and Lilliput.

speakers.name: Ron Pressler
speakers.bio: Ron is an architect in the Java Platform Group at Oracle

title: Build the Builder: A Java Coding Agent in Your IDE with ACP
summary: This session shows how to build a production-ready coding agent in Java/Kotlin, connect it to IntelliJ via ACP, and orchestrate external agents like Codex, Claude, and Gemini. It covers reasoning loops, tools, guardrails, IDE context, and coordinated multi-agent workflows for real software engineering tasks.

speakers.name: Vadim Briliantov
speakers.bio:
Technical Product Manager for the ACP Protocol and Agent Ecosystem at JetBrains.

Vadim is the creator and former Technical Lead of the Koog framework at JetBrains. Over the past 9 years at JetBrains, he has contributed to a wide range of projects, including the IntelliJ Kotlin plugin, Kotlin Libraries, the Ktor framework, Qodana Cloud Backend, and Multiplatform Tooling. He also led the technological direction of AI agent development across multiple products as part of the AI Agents Platform.
Today, Vadim is responsible for the ACP Protocol and Open Agent Ecosystem in JetBrains IDEs, driving the vision of making JetBrains IDEs the open gateway for integrating any external AI agents while augmenting them with JetBrains IDEs' deep code understanding and development capabilities.

title: Structured Concurrency Looms
summary: Structured Concurrency in Project Loom builds on virtual threads to simplify concurrent programming by treating related tasks as one unit. It improves cancellation, error handling, and observability, and makes code easier to understand and debug. The session covers its design, usage, evolution, and future lower-level API work.

speakers.name: Alan Bateman
speakers.bio: Alan Bateman is an architect in the Java Platform Group at Oracle and a long-time contributor to OpenJDK. He leads the OpenJDK Core Libraries Group and has helped shape the evolution of the Java platform through the design and implementation of many JDK features, including New I/O (NIO), JVMTI and serviceability, the Java Module System, and, more recently, Project Loom.

title: I Hired a Real Robot as My Junior Dev — and Now My Kids Don't Want to Learn Java Anymore
summary: A humorous talk on how AI agents and desktop robots may commoditize coding while increasing the value of architecture, systems thinking, and product judgment. It explores a shift from typing code to directing agents in natural language, asking whether we’re training the last generation of developers.

speakers.name: Jan Van Wassenhove
speakers.bio:
Jan Van Wassenhove is the Technical Director of the System Integrations Business Line for the BeLux region at Sopra Steria, where he drives technology solutions and services, supported by his team of architects. With a strong background in Java development, Jan has evolved into an experienced architect and project manager, with in-depth expertise in Agile methodologies.

Remarkably, he is also the initiator of “SCRUM”, a new programming language he conceived. This creation perfectly reflects his innovative mindset and constant drive to explore new technological territories — and proves, with a wink, that everyone really can become a SCRUM master… in code.

Throughout his career, he has contributed to numerous projects in both the public and private sectors, with a particular focus on banking and public administrations.

title: Post-Quantum Today: How Your Passwords Will Be Safe in a Quantum Future
summary: This talk explains RSA encryption, how Shor’s algorithm could break it, the current state of quantum hardware, and why post-quantum cryptography matters now. It also introduces lattice-based quantum-safe encryption and current adoption progress, helping audiences understand future cryptography and “harvest now, decrypt later” risks.

speakers.name: Julian Burr
speakers.bio: Senior Developer from Germany with over 15 years of experience building web apps and leading frontend teams, currently living and working down under in Australia. Pragmatic perfectionist, always looking for opportunities to learn and grow.

title: Emergent DevEx: The Good, the Bad, and the Legacy
summary: This talk explores how developer experience deteriorates as organizations scale, creating bureaucratic friction and outdated internal tools. It argues that copying DevEx models from companies like Google or Netflix is misguided, and offers strategies for engineers to shape and resist tool-driven bureaucracy.

speakers.name: Makan Sepehrifar
speakers.bio:
Makan Sepehrifar is a software architect who is interested in how people think and behave in organizations. He sees software architecture as a craft and believes that every challenge has both a technical side and a social side, and both need attention at the same time. Coming from a strong developer background, he has led many teams across different domains and organizations, always working to connect technology with human needs and team dynamics.
He is passionate about the future of Developer Experience and how Generative AI and Agentic AI are reshaping the way developers work. Makan focuses on how these technologies can improve developer satisfaction and help teams become more adaptive and effective. He is a public speaker on Developer Experience practices and AI in this space, and he has been part of several Generative AI adoption teams in different companies, helping them use AI in a practical and effective way.

speakers.name: Soroosh Khodami
speakers.bio: Soroosh is a software engineer and software architecture enthusiast, passionate about building simple but impactful solutions. With over 15 years of experience in diverse domains, including Telecom, Media & Entertainment, and E-Commerce. He has worked with small startups and large enterprises serving 80 million active subscribers. Currently working as a Solution Architect at Rabobank. Soroosh strongly believes in the power of collaborative learning and enjoys sharing his experiences and insights with other developers.

title: Fun with Flags: How OpenFeature Solves Your Feature Flag Headaches
summary: Feature flags improve agile software delivery, but complexity grows with targeting, multi-language support, vendor lock-in, and cleanup. This talk explores common feature flag pitfalls and shows how OpenFeature’s vendor-agnostic SDKs and tools simplify flag management and make the process easier.

speakers.name: Simon Schrottner
speakers.bio:
I help teams release faster and with more confidence — through open standards, feature flagging, and the communities that make both possible.

I am a software engineer and CNCF Ambassador based in Austria, and a maintainer of OpenFeature — the CNCF vendor-neutral standard for feature flagging. I contribute across the full organisation in Java, Python, Go, and JavaScript, spanning the open standard itself, testing automation across a polyglot environment, and guiding teams and individuals in adopting OpenFeature in production.

I am passionate about developer experience, open standards, and building communities where people help each other grow. I regularly speak at conferences and mentor individuals taking their first steps in the open source world.

title: MCP 2.0 - Stateless, New Auth (CIMD), and Exciting Extensions
summary: The session reviews recent MCP spec and implementation changes and their impact on server developers. It covers stateless transport, new CIMD authentication, and extensions like MCP Apps, Tasks, and Skills. Code examples and demos show how to build servers using the latest MCP features and approaches.

speakers.name: James Ward
speakers.bio: Professional software developer since 1997, with much of that time spent helping developers build software that doesn't suck. A Typed Pure Functional Programming zealot who often compromises on his ideals to just get stuff done. Currently a Developer Advocate for AWS and AAIF Technical Committee member.

title: Wrap, Reshape, or Redesign: Retrofitting Your APIs for a World of Agents
summary: The talk explores how to adapt human-designed APIs for LLM agents, which interpret instructions literally and need explicit boundaries. It presents a practical framework for retrofitting APIs into agent-ready tools, with real examples, tradeoffs, and cases where redesign improves both agent and human usability.

speakers.name: Horacio Gonzalez
speakers.bio:
Spaniard lost in Brittany, coder, speaker, dreamer and all-around geek.

Horacio is VP of DevRel at Clever Cloud. He is also the co-founder and leader of the FinistDevs and Rdv des Speakers communities.

Horacio loves web development in general and everything around Web Components and standards web in particular, but he also loves to discuss Kubernetes, AI and cloud in general.

title: Mission Possible: The 45-Minute Path to Bullet-Proof Java Container Images
summary: A lunch session on hardening Java container images by reducing CVE noise and operational risk. It covers choosing minimal base images, shrinking privileges, pinning versions, signing and SBOMs, using CVSS-based scanning, and automating updates with Dependabot/Renovate, with practical Dockerfile guidance and verification steps.

speakers.name: Pasha Finkelshtein
speakers.bio: Years of experience in software engineering and the team's leading roles combined with his passion for Java made Pasha know all the hidden details in this IT niche. As a Developer Advocate for @Bellsoft, he educates the public on the latest software tools built by BellSoft and helps to create and test instruments for developers. He writes in Kotlin, speaks at conferences, composes a new articles, or maintains his pet projects.

title: Life in the Ivory Tower: Confessions of a Former Developer Who Turned Into an Architect
summary: A humorous talk about becoming an enterprise architect and bridging the gap between hands-on development and corporate IT decision-making. It explores the psychology behind technical choices, staying technically current while moving up, and fostering collaboration between developers and architects.

speakers.name: Robin Custers
speakers.bio: Robin is a software architect at Cegeka, bringing over 20 years of experience in software development. He's progressed from developer to team coach to software architect, all while avoiding any serious coffee spills. Robin's expertise includes agile software development, extreme and not-always-so-extreme programming, domain-driven design and software architecture. He's a skilled at designing and implementing enterprise-class systems. He enjoys helping organisations achieve their strategic goals, one line of code at a time, making sure their IT dreams don’t turn into digital nightmares.

title: From User Prompt to JPA Query: Comparing Tool Calling, Structured Output & Hybrid Approach
summary: The project compares three LLM approaches for natural-language database filtering in a Java Spring AI/Vaadin app: function calling, structured output, and a hybrid method. Tested with local Ollama models, it evaluates reliability, speed, cost, and limitations for handling complex filter requests.

speakers.name: Sebastian Kühnau
speakers.bio: Sebastian has been a Java junkie for over two decades and fell in love with Vaadin during his university days. Since 2016, he has worked in various technical roles at Vaadin, helping customers build tailor-made web applications and leading workshops and training sessions. In 2024, he transitioned to looking after the community full-time, traveling from event to event as a speaker to share his knowledge and passion for Vaadin. When he’s not at a conference or experimenting with AI, he’s always up for a tech talk and a good cup of coffee.

title: Engineering for the Long Haul: Operating Open Source at Scale
summary: The presentation explains how enterprises can securely and compliantly manage open-source software over time despite short lifecycles and upgrade demands. It highlights TuxCare solutions—rebootless patching, end-of-life security updates, low-noise vulnerability scanning, and enterprise support—to extend software life and reduce risk.

speakers.name: Sven Sellen
speakers.bio:
Sven Sellen is a veteran of the cybersecurity and open-source industries, currently serving as the Director of Global Enterprise Sales at TuxCare, Inc. With a career spanning over 27 years, Sven has navigated the evolution of the digital landscape through executive leadership roles in Consulting, Sales Engineering, and Project Management.

As a high-level advocate for the Linux ecosystem, Sven specializes in bridging the gap between complex global enterprise infrastructure and robust security protocols.

At TuxCare, he leads the global sales strategy, helping multinational organizations manage the entire Linux lifecycle—from automated live patching to extended support for end-of-life systems—ensuring that mission-critical environments remain secure and compliant without the need for disruptive reboots.

Sven is a recognized Public Speaker at major international technology fairs and partner events. He is well-known for his ability to translate high-level security concepts into actionable global business strategies. His insights on Linux security, vulnerability management, and enterprise open-source trends have been featured in premier technical outlets, including heise online, Computerwoche, and it-security journal.

title: What rules the virtual? How our systems obey physical laws.
summary: This proposal explores the physical foundations of information and computation, asking how data is stored, moved, and erased in the real world. It examines energy, speed, and disappearance of information, then extends into quantum effects and how stable states emerge beneath digital abstractions.

speakers.name: Marianne Hoornenborg
speakers.company: NLJUG and KVK (Dutch Chamber of Commerce)
speakers.bio:
Marianne Hoornenborg is a Lead for the Dutch Java community NLJUG and works in the CIO Office at the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KVK) where she started her Java career a decade ago. She is passionate about promoting gender diversity and challenging stereotypes about our profession.

As an international speaker, Marianne explores the concepts that are hidden beneath the surface of the technology we use every day. Her talks invite curiosity, challenge assumptions and turn complex ideas into fun discoveries. She aims for the audience to enjoy her talks as much as she enjoyed preparing them.

title: Eval Driven Development: Why you need it to make your Agentic Application survive Production
summary: Eval-Driven Development (EDD) adapts test-driven development to agentic AI systems, helping manage hallucinations, drift, and workflow surprises. This talk shows how to build reliable agents with layered evals, golden datasets, rubrics, trace signals, and regression gates, using JVM AI frameworks like Spring AI, LangChain4J, and Koog.

speakers.name: Urs Peter
speakers.bio:
Urs is a seasoned software engineer, solution architect, conference speaker, and trainer with over 20 years of experience building resilient, scalable, and mission-critical systems, primarily in Kotlin, Scala, and Java. Lately, also agentic systems with JVM technology.

Besides his job as a consultant, he is also a passionate trainer and author of a wide range of courses, including language courses for Kotlin and Scala, generative AI courses for the JVM platform, as well as architectural trainings on Microservices and Event-Driven Architectures.

As a people person by nature, he loves to share knowledge, inspire, and be inspired by peers at meetups and conferences. Urs is a JetBrains-certified Kotlin trainer.

title: Safety, speed, and governance in the agentic era
summary: The session explores Docker Sandboxes as a secure local isolation layer for AI agents, limiting filesystem and credential access. It also addresses how agents can still leak data, and proposes a multi-layered approach combining sandboxing, tool governance, and policy controls for safer, trustworthy agent execution.

speakers.name: Oleg Šelajev
speakers.bio: Oleg is nice and great, and knows many things about software development, AI and other cool things.

title: Run Frontier Open Models on consumer hardware
summary: A deep dive into fast, production-grade on-device inference on Macs using the MLX ecosystem. Covers unified memory, continuous batching, KV-cache compression, speculative decoding, and model porting pitfalls, with real benchmark results and engineering tradeoffs for balancing accuracy, latency, and memory on consumer hardware.

speakers.name: Prince Canuma
speakers.bio: Prince Canuma is Founder and CEO of Neywa Labs, building the inference stack for Apple Silicon. He is the creator and primary maintainer of the MLX open-source ecosystem — mlx-vlm, mlx-audio, and mlx-embeddings — with over 4M combined downloads, foundational to on-device AI on Apple hardware. He previously led developer experience at Neptune AI and worked at Arcee on post-training and inference optimization. His work focuses on model optimization and making AI accessible on local hardware.

title: 🌉 Gateway API, 10 years of maturation for a new Kubernetes network API
summary: The text introduces Kubernetes network exposure challenges and explains how the new standard Gateway API aims to simplify them. It covers standard and proprietary options, advanced features, available implementations, and how to install Gateway API in a cluster.

speakers.name: Kevin Davin
speakers.bio:
Google Developer Expert on Google Cloud & Kotlin, Gitlab Hero, I am above all passionate about tech, languages, infrastructure, and automation.

On a daily basis, I work with languages such as Kotlin, Java, SQL, and YAML.
Leveraging the power of the Google Kubernetes Engine and GitLab's Continuous Integration, I deploy and manage applications seamlessly.

I am an ardent advocate of agility and DevOps, and I had the privilege of guiding teams in adopting these principles successfully.

From code quality analysis to unit or end-to-end tests setup all the way to continuous deployment and operation, I ensure a project's journey from inception to production is smooth and efficient.

Currently, I'm Principal Software Engineer at Gradle, focusing on the development of Develocity. This groundbreaking product enhances developer productivity by reducing build and test times, while also providing valuable insights into all aspects of the development process.

title: The pizza party of the future 🍕 software teams and product value in the age of coding agents
summary: AI is reshaping software teams, creating new bottlenecks around value and trust. The talk explores how developer roles, team structures, and responsibilities may evolve—from cross-functional teams to AI-assisted models—drawing on past agile critiques to imagine a more value-driven future of human-agent collaboration.

speakers.name: Katie Clark
speakers.bio:
Katie is a delivery lead, manager, (ex) software developer, and trainer at Reply Comsysto. Over the past 8 years, she has been involved in complex software projects spanning various domains, from semiconductor manufacturing to food supply chains.
Developing quality software products requires a team effort. Therefore, her focus is on fostering a collaborative team culture, promoting an agile mindset, and continuously evolving suitable processes within the organization.

speakers.name: Simon Rohrer
speakers.bio:
Simon Rohrer, Head of Enterprise Architecture and Ways of Working at Saxo Bank has spent his career advocating for modern ways of working, with roles in hands on software engineering, agile coaching with a focus on technical excellence, and senior roles in enterprise architecture and strategy.

He's a co-author of Jonathan Smart's IT Revolution Press book Sooner Safer Happier, and working on a chapter on organising for outcomes for the forthcoming follow-up book.

title: G1, ZGC, Shenandoah, ... with all these GCs in Java, which one do I choose?
summary: This talk explains why Java has multiple garbage collectors, what ZGC, Shenandoah, and others do, and their strengths and weaknesses. It traces GC history, compares alternatives, and shows when to use each one for the right project, application, or environment.

speakers.name: Antoine DESSAIGNE
speakers.bio:
A Java developer with over 20 years of experience, Antoine has been a key part of Axway since 2012.

He dedicated 13 years to their Analytics software, evolving from developer to software architect while maintaining a hands-on development role. His final five years on the project were focused on performance optimization, cloud migration, and security.

Antoine is passionate about open source and reports bugs to community-driven projects. He is always eager to migrate to the latest JDK and introduce new features to his team.

Today, he is leveraging his expertise to build an AI Gateway solution, tackling complex code, and mentoring others.

title: Deterministic by Design - Achieving Reproducible Builds with Maven
summary: This session shows how Apache Maven can make builds reproducible by producing identical artifacts from identical inputs. It explains how to diagnose non-determinism, use Maven’s verification tools, and improve traceability and compliance in software delivery pipelines increasingly scrutinized by auditors and regulators.

speakers.name: Maarten Mulders
speakers.bio: Maarten is a solution architect, senior Java developer, and technical trainer with a passion for developer productivity and software quality. He is recognised as a Java Champion and Oracle ACE Pro for his contributions to the Java community through speaking, mentoring, and content creation. Maarten is passionate about "building the right thing" and "building the thing right". He loves to share new ideas and knowledge through speaking and his blog. When he's not writing code or speaking at conferences, Maarten enjoys exploring creativity through photography, music, and experimenting in the kitchen - in no particular order.

title: A Year of Agentic AI Evolution: Lessons Learned Building Production-grade Agentic Systems
summary: LangChain4j’s agentic framework has evolved from fixed patterns to flexible orchestration, letting developers compose strategies for different use cases. The session covers new built-in patterns, their trade-offs, and production features like tracing, state persistence, failure recovery, and human-in-the-loop pauses.

speakers.name: Mario Fusco
speakers.bio: Mario is a senior principal software engineer at IBM working as Drools project lead. Among his interests there are also high performance systems and generative AI, being an active contributor of widely adopted projects like Quarkus and LangChain4j. He is also a Java Champion, the JUG Milano coordinator, a frequent speaker and the co-author of "Modern Java in Action" published by Manning.

speakers.name: Kevin Dubois
speakers.bio: Kevin Dubois is a software architect and platform engineer with a career spanning over 20 years. He is often featured as a keynote speaker at conferences around the world where he shares his experience and knowledge about cloud native & AI software development, developer experience, open source and Java. Kevin is also an author and Java Champion. He currently works as a Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM, and is  Technical Lead for the CNCF Developer Experience Technical Advisory Group as well as an ambassador for the Agentic AI Foundation.

title: Harness Engineering: Building the System Around Your AI Coding Agent
summary: AI coding agents are fundamentally simple: prompt a model, execute tool calls, feed results back, and repeat. This talk builds such an engine in Java, then iteratively adds context, constraints, and feedback to show how real tools improve reliability, safety, and understanding of their limits.

speakers.name: JI Darwish
speakers.bio: Ji is a Data Platform Engineer at Xomnia with a background in Computer Science & Engineering from TU Delft and a recently completed MSc in Artificial Intelligence from Utrecht University. With years of experience in software development, he focuses on solving real-world software and data problems, while maintaining a strong interest in AI, education, and emerging digital policy. He is particularly drawn to questions around EU sovereign tech, AI alignment, and how to build systems that are not only capable, but also compliant, trustworthy, and grounded in human values. Driven by the belief that technology, when built thoughtfully, can be a genuine force for good, Ji is passionate about the role AI can play in improving learning experiences and advancing society responsibly.

title: Java, Raspberry Pi, and the Art of Overengineering Everyday Life
summary: Java developers can build practical Raspberry Pi home automation without leaving their tools. This talk shows two real projects—a BBQ smoker controller and a jetty server for photos, water levels, and fishing alerts—covering hardware access, deployment, reliable services, mobile UIs, and secure remote control.

speakers.name: Matti Tahvonen
speakers.bio: Matti Tahvonen has worked on web apps for over two decades. Vaadin’s first-ever JavaScript developer, he has evolved into a Java/JVM enthusiast over the years while working with an open-source Java web framework and building a business around it. When Matti isn’t working, he spends most of his time on nature-related hobbies—and on developing software to support them.

title: Integration patterns for distributed systems
summary: The session explains distributed-systems challenges in modern interconnected applications—such as retries, idempotence, ordering, and failures—and the design trade-offs and patterns used to manage them. It targets architects, developers, and executives, and offers guidance for modernizing legacy systems into loosely coupled, flexible, scalable architectures.

speakers.name: Dirk Fröhner
speakers.bio: In his role as Principal Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services, Dirk Fröhner works with software companies on their multi-dimensional transformation. Target areas include technology and software architecture evolution, organizational change, and innovation culture. For this, he contributes his wealth of professional experience and knowledge of human nature, all of which he gained from 25+ years in the business. Dirk's favorite software architecture topic is everything around integration architecture, both in theory and practice: After all, most considerations of building software systems turn out to be integration problems - particularly when it comes to distributed systems. He keeps speaking about this at tech conferences globally, including flagship events like AWS re:Invent. In his spare time, Dirk is a pain-resistant supporter of Schalke 04.

speakers.name: Sabarish Sekar
speakers.bio:
Sabarish Sekar is an ISV Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services, where he helps independent software vendors accelerate innovation and modernize their platforms on AWS. With over 13 years of hands-on experience as a developer and solutions architect spanning healthcare and financial services, he brings a practitioner's perspective to solving complex architectural challenges.
Sabarish is passionate about building resilient, scalable systems using serverless technologies, event-driven integration patterns, and the emerging possibilities of Agentic AI. He enjoys breaking down complex topics into practical, actionable guidance that engineering teams can apply immediately.

Topics I Speak About

  • Serverless architectures for ISVs and SaaS platforms
  • Integration patterns for distributed systems and event-driven design
  • Agentic AI and how software companies can harness autonomous AI workflows
  • Modernization journeys from monolith to cloud-native

title: Teaching an Old Handle New Tricks: From Core Reflection to FFM
summary: The talk explains how Java reflection is inefficient, and how method handles and var handles create reusable, typed capabilities that better match JVM linkage. It also shows how this design supports newer APIs like Foreign Function & Memory and serialization, illustrating resilient platform design.

speakers.name: Maurizio Cimadamore
speakers.bio:
Maurizio Cimadamore is a compiler architect at Oracle. He is currently working on the language and runtime aspects of many foundational projects that will change the shape of the Java platform, such as Project Valhalla and Project Panama.
In the previous years, he has contributed to the design and implementation of several features of the Java programming language, such as diamond inference, lambda expressions and local variable type-inference. Maurizio holds a PhD in language design and implementation.

speakers.name: Viktor Klang
speakers.bio:
Viktor is a Software Architect in the Java Platform Group at Oracle.

For more than two decades, he has focused on enabling developers to solve problems with maximal productivity and maintainability.

Specializing in developer ergonomics in the realm of concurrent, parallel, and distributed programming; he has contributed to the standard libraries of several major programming languages, been involved in more than a dozen Open Source projects, and has spoken at numerous conferences and universities.

title: 0 to 350 Engineers on Claude Code: What Could Go Wrong?
summary: AI coding agents are transforming software development, enabling non-developers to build features and teams to work end-to-end. The talk explores real-world adoption, risks like large uncontrolled changes, cost management, and how developers and organizations must adapt to prompting, agents, skills, and CI/CD.

speakers.name: Nicolas Martignole
speakers.bio:
Nicolas is a Principal Engineer at Back Market, a leader in refurbished electronic devices in 18 countries. He is also the co-creator and organizer of Devoxx France. He has a JVM background but has worked in different industries and technologies. Before joining Back Market, he was a Principal Engineer at Doctolib, during the COVID19 crisis.
He's also the author of "le Touilleur Express", a blog about the journey of a software developer.
He has a YouTube Channel with more than 800 subscribers, on GenAI and Coding Agent.

title: CRAcking Compliance - The EU Cyber Resilience Act
summary: The talk explains the EU Cyber Resilience Act, its impact, and new compliance requirements. It covers SBOM generation for Java, .NET, and JavaScript projects, CI integration, vulnerability management with Dependabot/Renovate, and reducing risk through automated dependency updates and distroless images.

speakers.name: Christian Schabetsberger
speakers.bio:
Christian Schabetsberger, the world's okayest developer, is a Freelance Software Engineer & Architect from Linz, Austria with over a decade of experience.
Having spend half of his life in the .NET ecosystem (amongst others), he likes to stay on the bleeding edge of technology to become the (tech-savvy) ninja he pretends to be since he is six.
He is also an active community member, organising the .NET Meetup in Linz and supporting other local user groups. Furthermore he is a member of the .NET Foundation.

title: Pragmatic multi-cloud architecture: designing for resilience and portability beyond the hype
summary: This session explores designing a real-world multi-cloud platform, weighing the benefits of using multiple providers against challenges like latency, fragmented data, incompatible APIs, security, and SLA risks. It covers bounded contexts, production hurdles, API design, best practices, and pragmatic risk analysis to guide coherent architecture decisions.

speakers.name: Alexandre Touret
speakers.bio:
With over two decades of experience as a seasoned software architect, I am fueled by a passion for technology, cloud computing, and software development. Throughout my career, I have designed, built, and managed systems of varying scales across a diverse range of industries, including insurance, financial services, and mobility.

I take great pleasure in sharing my insights and experiences with others, whether by teaching, speaking at conferences, organizing hands-on workshops, or writing articles. By engaging with the community, I aim to inspire and provide practical insights drawn from my hands-on experience.

title: Bootiful Spring Boot 4
summary: Explore Spring Boot 4.x with Java 25+, covering scalable, modular, secure, and intelligent applications. Learn about the Spring ecosystem, AI integration, seamless data access, and production optimizations including virtual threads, Project Leyden, GraalVM, and more for building faster, more efficient systems.

speakers.name: Josh Long
speakers.bio: Josh (@starbuxman) has been the first Spring Developer Advocate since 2010. Josh is a Java Champion, author of 7 books (including "Reactive Spring") and numerous best-selling video training (including "Building Microservices with Spring Boot Livelessons"with Spring Boot co-founder Phil Webb), and an open-source contributor (Spring Boot, Spring Integration, Axon, Spring Cloud, Activiti, Vaadin, etc), a Youtuber (Coffee + Software with Josh Long as well as my Spring Tips series ), and a podcaster ("A Bootiful Podcast").

title: How to survive and thrive as a dev (team) in the exponential age of AI. Real-world AI adoption, smarter ways of working, and lessons from the front lines
summary: Sander Hoogendoorn shares a practical, no-hype view of AI at iBOOD: how it’s reshaping product architecture, engineering, and team culture. He covers real risks like lock-in and fragile dependencies, and explains why autonomous microteams, experimentation, and adaptability replace traditional processes in the AI era.

speakers.name: Sander Hoogendoorn
speakers.bio:
Sander Hoogendoorn is an independent dad, avid traveler, and lifelong software developer. With over 40 years of hands-on coding experience under his belt, he still ships code every day — because once a developer, always a developer.

Currently the CTO at iBOOD, Sander has led technology at several companies over the past decade and was once Capgemini’s global agile thought leader. But don’t expect corporate buzzwords — Sander’s known for cutting through the fluff with a post-agile mindset and a healthy disregard for outdated best practices.

He helps teams and organizations break rules that need breaking — replacing heavyweight processes with lightweight thinking, and agile dogma with actual flow. If something’s slowing your team down, chances are he’s already ranted about it in a keynote.

Onstage, Sander brings code, stories, and sharp insights — whether he’s talking disruption, continuous delivery, microservices, monads (yes, really), software architecture, or the lost art of writing beautiful code. His talks are fast-paced, thought-provoking, and never just theory.

Sander believes in small steps, critical thinking, and building stuff that works. No silver bullets. Just better software, made by better teams.

title: Why Documentation Won’t Write Itself—and AI Won’t Save You
summary: The talk argues that AI won’t solve poor documentation. It presents practical principles for keeping docs close to code, separating architecture/API/code-level documentation, and preventing decay. Key takeaway: missing context remains missing unless teams make deliberate documentation decisions first.

speakers.name: Christian Heitzmann
speakers.bio: Christian Heitzmann, MSc ETH CSE, is the owner of SimplexaCode AG in Lucerne, Switzerland. His professional certifications include Java, Python, and Spring. He holds teaching diplomas in both Computer Science and Mathematics, as well as a CAS in Machine Learning. With over 20 years of experience in professional software development and over 15 years in teaching and training, he works as a developer, documentation consultant, and trainer, bringing order to software, documentation, and data.

title: Building LLM Inference Engines in Java with TornadoVM and the NVIDIA Ecosystem
summary: The session shows how Java can run GPU-accelerated local LLMs natively with TornadoVM, using NVIDIA libraries without JNI. It covers GPULlama3.java, quantized inference, Quarkus and LangChain4J integration, and how TornadoVM plus Project Babylon/Panama position Java as a strong AI and HPC platform.

speakers.name: Thanos Stratikopoulos
speakers.bio: Dr. Athanasios Stratikopoulos (male) is a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester with specialization on heterogeneous architectures and reconfigurable accelerators. He has authored more than 20 research articles in the field of hardware acceleration, system software and programming languages. Currently his work involves heterogeneous architectures ranging from low-power devices to high-end cloud deployments. He is one of the lead developers of TornadoVM and has been part of the team for the last eight years. In addition to his core contributions to the system's technical development, Dr. Stratikopoulos leads the project's communication and dissemination efforts, helping to articulate its goals and advancements to both academic and industrial audiences through talks, documentation, and outreach activities.

speakers.name: Michalis Papadimitriou
speakers.bio:
Michalis Papadimitriou is a Senior Software Engineer at Neo4j and a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester. His core expertise includes open-source software development, hardware abstractions for high-level programming languages, compiler optimizations for GPU computing, and enabling large language model (LLM) inference on GPUs for the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
He is focused on advancing high-performance AI and graph computing systems, with particular interest in GPU acceleration for machine learning workloads on the JVM through the TornadoVM framework, and continues to actively maintain the open-source GPULlama3.java project.
Before joining Neo4j, Michalis was a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester, where he contributed to the TornadoVM project as a Staff Software Engineer. Prior to that, he worked across a range of software stacks at Huawei Technologies and contributed to the open-source machine learning compiler Apache TVM while at OctoAI (formerly OctoML), which was later acquired by NVIDIA.

speakers.name: Orion Papadakis
speakers.bio: TornadoVM

title: Surviving the "AI Slopageddon": How AI shakes the foundations of Open Source
summary: Vibe Coding boosts productivity but overwhelms open-source maintainers with low-quality AI-generated pull requests, hallucinated bug reports, and autonomous agents. This talk examines AI’s existential threat to open source and proposes defensive strategies such as stricter access, restructuring workflows, and machine-adapted governance.

speakers.name: Raphael Semeteys
speakers.bio:
I am a technologist and Content Producer with over 25 years of experience across software engineering, open-source communities, and emerging tech. My current focus is on the frontiers of Generative AI, specifically local LLMs, image generation (Stable Diffusion), and Agentic AI.

Throughout my career, I’ve balanced technical leadership with a passion for knowledge sharing. I created the QSOS method for open source evaluation and recently explored the intersection of "vibe-coding" and storytelling by publishing AI-assisted techno-thrillers.

A frequent speaker at international conferences like Devoxx, Open Source Experience, and various DevFests, I enjoy deconstructing complex ecosystems—from Web3 architecture to multimodal AI—into clear, actionable insights. I also bring a unique perspective to tech by integrating holistic yoga practices into my approach to innovation and engineering.

More about me: https://raphiki.github.io/

title: AI Made Building Cheap. Now Decisions Are the Bottleneck.
summary: AI is making software delivery faster, shifting the main bottleneck from execution to decision-making. This talk shows how AI can improve discovery, architecture, and delivery conversations, turning discussions into maps, diagrams, risks, and options to expose complexity, align stakeholders, and make better decisions.

speakers.name: Dave Sammut
speakers.bio:
Dave Sammut is a Principal Consultant and Head of Architecture (EMEA) at Equal Experts, where he helps organisations tackle complex technology, architecture, and transformation challenges. With more than 20 years of experience in software delivery, he has worked across banking, insurance, retail, telecommunications, healthcare, and public sector organisations, helping teams modernise systems, improve delivery effectiveness, and navigate large-scale change.
Dave specialises in bridging the gap between business strategy and technical execution through Domain-Driven Design, software architecture, Team Topologies, collaborative discovery, and modern engineering practices. His work focuses on helping organisations uncover hidden assumptions, reduce risk, and make better decisions before investing in implementation.
In recent years, Dave has been exploring how AI is reshaping software delivery. His work examines the growing shift from execution as the primary constraint to decision quality, judgement, and governance becoming the critical differentiators for successful teams. He regularly advises organisations on the practical application of AI across architecture, software delivery, and organisational design.
Alongside his consulting work, Dave is an experienced conference speaker, workshop facilitator, and former part-time radio presenter. He is known for combining real-world consulting experiences with engaging storytelling, practical examples, and interactive demonstrations that challenge conventional thinking about technology and software delivery.
Whether working with engineering teams, architects, or senior leaders, Dave's passion lies in helping people navigate complexity, align around shared understanding, and deliver meaningful outcomes with confidence.

speakers.name: João Rosa
speakers.bio:
João Rosa helps organizations unlock more value with their teams and technology. He works with executives and senior leaders to transform and evolve the operating model so that teams are prepared to thrive in a turbulent environment. He has led transformations across financial services, telco, and retail.

He is a software engineer at heart, crossing technology problems with social enterprise challenges.

title: GraalVM Next: Layers, Crema, and WebAssembly in Action
summary: The session explores three GraalVM Native Image projects: Native Image Layers for shared code and memory, Project Crema for dynamic class loading at runtime, and Web Image for compiling JVM apps to WebAssembly for browsers. Together, they expand packaging, runtime behavior, and deployment targets.

speakers.name: Alina Yurenko
speakers.bio: Alina is a developer advocate for GraalVM at Oracle. Loves both programming and natural languages, compilers and performance, and open source. Ambassador of snacks and not running.

title: Building an Agent Ready Platform
summary: This session explains how to move AI agents from demo to production using platform engineering: secure model access, agent identity, inherited guardrails, and observability for actions and cost. It shows what developers should ask for from platform teams, and what platform teams should build first.

speakers.name: Timo Salm
speakers.bio: Timo Salm is a Principal Solutions Engineer at VMware Tanzu by Broadcom with over a decade of experience in customer-facing roles, modern applications, DevSecOps, and AI. In his roles, he ensures that the most strategic customers in the EMEA region achieve their goals with VMware Tanzu's Spring, developer platform, AI, and data products. Another essential part of his role is continuously learning through experimenting hands-on with innovations and sharing the outcomes with colleagues, customers, and the community via, for example, conferences. Before Timo joined Pivotal, which VMware and now Broadcom acquired, he worked for consulting firms in the automotive industry as a software architect and full-stack developer.

title: Architecture Observability and Guardrails
summary: Talk on preventing “AI slop” by enforcing code quality in AI-generated codebases. It covers agent design feedback loops and ways to preserve human review bandwidth, using C4 models, PlantUML, captured sequence diagrams, complexity visualizations, and efficient testing practices.

speakers.name: Victor Rentea
speakers.bio: With 2 decades of software engineering experience, Victor spent the last 10 years training thousands of developers and architects from 150+ companies. Since early 2026, he’s been working hard to help his clients adopt Agentic Engineering, coaching AI Champions, developers, testers, product owners, ops, and managers with practical, actionable advice to kick-start their agentic reconversion. Every year, Victor gives energetic, intense conference talks in which he distills his training sessions - so be sure not to miss these ideas, heavily brainstormed with millennia of total experience. More about him on https://victorrentea.ro, and https://agentic.how.

title: Consistency Patterns in Event-Driven Architecture
summary: This talk explains how to avoid inconsistencies in distributed systems caused by dual writes and failed transactions. It covers Outbox/Inbox patterns, idempotent consumers, and Saga orchestration/choreography, showing when to use each and the trade-offs involved with eventual consistency.

speakers.name: Emanuel Trandafir
speakers.bio:
Hey there, I'm Emanuel - a Software Craftsman from Romania.

I value simplicity and intentionality over blindly applying patterns and abstractions.

I care deeply about the design and testability of the software I create.

I also value communication and collaboration and enjoy sharing my knowledge through open-source contributions and technical articles.

title: Big Runtimes Make Efficient Programs
summary: Large runtimes, like the JVM, can improve both convenience and performance by enabling JIT compilation and garbage collection. This challenges the idea that smaller runtimes and more compile-time decisions are always faster, showing the real tradeoffs are more complex.

speakers.name: Ron Pressler
speakers.bio: Ron is an architect in the Java Platform Group at Oracle

title: Quarkus Meets Leyden at the JVM Performance Edge
summary: This talk shares hands-on Quarkus experiments with Project Leyden, exploring how Leyden’s JVM startup and warm-up improvements interact with Quarkus’ build-time optimizations. It highlights what works, current limitations, performance findings, broken assumptions, and design changes needed to combine both approaches effectively.

speakers.name: Georgios Andrianakis
speakers.bio:
Georgios works for IBM as a Senior Principal Software Engineer and is currently one of the most active contributors to Quarkus, where he works in all sorts of areas, including but not limited to LangChain4j, RESTEasy Reactive, Spring compatibility, Kubernetes support, testing, Kotlin, and more.

He is also an enthusiastic promoter of Quarkus who never misses a chance to spread the Quarkus love!

speakers.name: Ana-Maria Mihalceanu
speakers.bio: Ana is a Java Champion Alumni and Senior Developer Advocate for the Java Platform Group at Oracle, with an extensive background in Java and cloud development. More recently, her work has expanded to explore how machine learning and AI can be applied within the Java ecosystem, helping Java developers adopt emerging capabilities while continuing to benefit from the stability, tooling, and performance of the Java Platform. She actively supports the growth of technical communities through knowledge sharing and enjoys curating content for conferences as a program committee member.

title: No Country For Old APIs. Wrapping legacy Java services as MCP tools without rewriting them.
summary: A demo-driven session on connecting AI agents to legacy Java, REST, and SOAP enterprise systems using MCP, Spring AI, and GraphQL. It tackles real brownfield challenges—auth, tool sprawl, oversized responses, and unsafe retries—and offers reusable patterns for secure, practical integration.

speakers.name: Željko Kozina
speakers.bio:
Željko has spent over 15 years in IT, mostly consulting for banks and insurance companies, with a focus on modernising legacy systems. Along the way, he developed deep expertise in JVM-based technologies and has become a go-to voice on topics such as API design. When he's not untangling someone else's technical debt, he's happily creating his own through a growing collection of personal projects he enthusiastically starts and occasionally finishes. Željko is passionate about sharing knowledge in a way that actually sticks, which usually means keeping things practical, a little entertaining, and free of unnecessary jargon.
He is a GraphQL Ambassador and a member of the GraphQL AI Working Group

title: Create your own AI Agents without code
summary: Docker Agent is an open-source, no-code platform for creating specialized AI agents quickly and affordably. It supports testing, benchmarking, optimization, and collaborative multi-agent workflows, while working with any LLM provider.

speakers.name: David Gageot
speakers.bio: Engineer at Docker, working an AI agents.

title: Beyond encryption at rest: computing on encrypted data
summary: This talk explains Homomorphic Encryption, which enables computation on encrypted data without decryption. It covers core concepts, modern Fully Homomorphic Encryption, practical applications in confidential AI, healthcare, and finance, and current limitations such as performance, ciphertext size, and implementation complexity.

speakers.name: Andrea Iacono
speakers.bio: Andrea is a software engineer with a broad experience in several industries ranging from e-commerce to industrial automation, from public administration to Web TV / music. His interests are in algorithms, data and AI.

title: When benchmarks go bad - what we learned from measuring performance wrong
summary: This talk explores common performance measurement mistakes, cognitive biases, and misleading intuitions. Franz and Holly explain why performance testing matters, how it can go wrong, and offer practical guidance for improving application performance, including test system setup, load generators, and the USE method.

speakers.name: Francesco Nigro
speakers.bio:
I've been working for many years in the computer field. In the last 15 years I've cultivated a strong passion in Java development and the under the hood details of OpenJDK, C and (x86) Assembly.
Big fan of DDD (Domain Driven Design) world, I've developed several Event-Sourcing high performance solutions in the medical and IoT field.
I'm an active member of various online communities on performance (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/mechanical-sympathy), Senior Principal (Software) Performance Engineer and Performance Lead for Red Hat/IBM on Quarkus, Red Hat Top Inventor (2019).
I've collaborated to different projects related high-performance computing both as committer and contributors eg Quarkus, Vert-x, Netty committer, JCTools author, PMC of ActiveMQ Apache Artemis (Messaging Broker), HdrHistogram, JGroups-raft, ...

speakers.name: Holly Cummins
speakers.bio:
Holly Cummins is a Senior Technical Staff Member on the IBM Quarkus team and a Java Champion. Over her career, Holly has been a full-stack javascript developer, a build architect, a client-facing consultant, a JVM performance engineer, and an innovation leader. Holly has led projects to understand climate risks, count fish, help a blind athlete run ultra-marathons in the desert solo, and invent stories (although not at all the same time). She gets worked up about sustainability, technical empathy, extreme programming, the importance of proper testing, and automating all the things. You can find her at https://hollycummins.com, or follow her on socials at @holly_cummins.

Over her career, Holly has been a full-stack javascript developer, a build architect, a client-facing consultant, a JVM performance engineer, and an innovation leader. Holly has led projects to understand climate risks, count fish, help a blind athlete run ultra-marathons in the desert solo, and invent stories (although not at all the same time). She gets worked up about sustainability, technical empathy, extreme programming, the importance of proper testing, and automating all the things. You can find her at http://hollycummins.com, or follow her on socials at @holly_cummins.

title: rm -rf self-doubt: Debugging Impostor Syndrome for Developers
summary: This session explains the neuroscience behind imposter syndrome in software teams and offers practical strategies to manage self-doubt, respond better to feedback, and grow through discomfort. Attendees will gain immediately usable tools for code reviews, design discussions, and stepping into larger roles.

speakers.name: Vincent Mayers
speakers.bio:
Expat Brit, artist, athlete, traveler, and technology community junkie. Vincent works as a Senior Community Manager at Neo4j, is a Java Champion, a steering committee member of MicroProfile, a board member of the Atlanta Java Users Group since 2008, and runs Devnexus, which is the largest community AI/Java conference in the USA.

Vincent has a degree in 3D Design from the University of Wolverhampton, United Kingdom, and, in another life, was a full-time athlete competing at World Championship level in whitewater kayaking.

title: Kubernetes for Developers
summary: Kubernetes for developers: what you need to know, without becoming a Kubernetes expert.

speakers.name: Alain Regnier
speakers.bio:
Alain Regnier is a Technical Architect and Entrepreneur passionate about innovation and new technologies.
He is a Kubestronaut and GDE Cloud (Google Developer Expert).

He works as Technical Director of the Kubernetes & DevOps group at SCIAM, a company providing Expertise Consulting Services.
Before that he was CTO for Kubo Labs, a company specialized in Kubernetes on premise and on the Cloud.

He helps companies that want to move to Kubernetes or use it more efficiently following Best Practices. (strategy, cluster installation, applications update, training, audit...)

He has also spent 10 years in Silicon Valley working for startups and large companies, where he co-authored various standards about Web Services and Connected Devices.

title: A Deserter Returns: What the Java community helped me rediscover
summary: A developer explains leaving Java for Python, then rediscovering Java through picocli, Quarkus, and TamboUI. The talk explores Java’s modern CLI, fast native apps, and terminal UIs, showing how community and new tooling made Java relevant again.

speakers.name: Thierry Chantier
speakers.bio:
A passion born from reading, the world of computing and electronics caught me from my ZX Spectrum and has never let go.
A developer by trade, from video games to master data management, I've also dabbled in the worlds of QA and production deployment.
I'm now a Developer Advocate at Dataiku, juggling between tech, community, and knowledge sharing.

Since a passion always deserves to be passed on, I founded Mixteen to try to help children grasp the digital world.
This desire to share has also led me to take part in organizing several MiXiT conferences and then to join the board of the AFPy.
In parallel, I also try to share through blog posts and videos on my YouTube channel.

In short:
https://calm.show/talks/

In detail:
https://www.twitch.tv/titimoby
https://mixteen.org/
https://tontoncodeur.fr/
https://www.youtube.com/thierrychantier
https://www.afpy.org

title: GraalVM Community BOF
summary: Join GraalVM core members for updates on Crema, enabling dynamic class loading in Native Image, and news across GraalOS, GraalPy, GraalWasm, Micronaut, and the broader ecosystem. This community BOF invites questions, feedback, and ideas to help shape GraalVM’s future.

speakers.name: Thomas Wuerthinger
speakers.bio: Thomas Wuerthinger is a Vice President at Oracle leading programming language implementation teams for languages including Python, JavaScript, and Java. He is the architect of the Graal compiler and the Truffle self-optimizing runtime system. Previously, he worked on the Crankshaft optimizing compiler of V8 at Google, and the Maxine research virtual machine at Sun Microsystems. He received a PhD degree from JKU Linz for his research about dynamic code evolution.

speakers.name: Fabio Niephaus
speakers.bio: Fabio Niephaus is a senior research manager on the GraalVM project at Oracle. He works on GraalPy, GraalWasm, and other Graal Languages, GraalVM Native Image, developer tools, and the overall GraalVM developer experience.

speakers.name: Shaun Smith
speakers.bio: Shaun has been a member of the Java community for over 25 years and has presented at many developer conferences and user groups around the world. He’s brought multiple Java application deployment cloud services to market and has been an active participant in multiple open source projects including GraalVM and the Java Persistence API (JPA) reference implementation, EclipseLink. Shaun currently leads Graal developer relations and product at Oracle.

title: Getting started with speaking: Your first conference talk
summary: This session, led by experienced speakers, offers practical guidance on starting technical speaking: choosing topics, writing proposals, preparing talks, and delivering effectively. It shares lessons learned, successes, failures, and key takeaways to help attendees begin their own speaking journey.

speakers.name: Bert Jan Schrijver
speakers.bio: Bert Jan is CTO at OpenValue and focuses on Java, AI, software architecture, Continuous Delivery and DevOps. Bert Jan is a Java Champion, JavaOne Rock Star speaker, Duke's Choice Award winner and leads NLJUG, the Dutch Java User Group. He loves to share his experience by speaking at conferences, writing for the Dutch Java magazine and helping out Devoxx4Kids with teaching kids how to code. Bert Jan is easily reachable on BlueSky via @bjschrijver.dev.

title: Rewriting the rules: How AI transforms engineering and inspiring young minds
summary: This talk shows how AI drives innovation in regulated banking, improving developer productivity through agentic automation, prompt libraries and Copilot. It also highlights social impact via Devoxx4Kids, where engineers built playful coding and cybersecurity learning platforms for children, inspiring the next generation.

speakers.name: Ayoub Hammou Ahabchane
speakers.bio:
IT Engineer with 13+ years of experience evolving across multiple roles, from Operations to Team Leadership, Project Management, and currently Lead Java Engineer.
My journey has given me a strong end to end understanding of systems, delivery, and people management.
I bring a hands-on technical mindset combined with leadership and ownership, enabling me to bridge the gap between business needs and engineering execution.

speakers.name: Kamel Zaraoui
speakers.bio:
Curious by nature, enthusiastic about new technologies, and always ready to take on challenges with a positive mindset.

For the past 8 years, I have been developing backend and frontend applications using Spring Boot and Lit HTML, with a strong focus on quality, performance, and user experience.

Alongside my work, I have a strong passion for cybersecurity, knowledge sharing, and artificial intelligence. I combined these three areas to design awareness workshops accessible to young audiences (from age 10 and up). The goal is to clearly and simply illustrate online risks — such as phishing, deepfakes, public Wi-Fi, VPNs, authentication, and SSL — and help them understand what is dangerous and what is not.

To support this educational approach, I leveraged AI to build an interactive platform accessible to everyone: 👉 https://kamelzar.github.io/CyberQuestKids/html/workshop.html#

title: Software Monuments - Architectural Lessons from the Systems That Shaped Computing
summary: The talk explores landmark software systems—Linux, Apollo Guidance Computer, Java, Deep Blue, the World Wide Web, and ELIZA—to reveal enduring architectural principles behind their success and show how these lessons can inspire modern software design.

speakers.name: Tobias Voss
speakers.bio: Tobias works as a modernization architect at viadee consulting. He supports customers in the modernization of their software architecture and the migration of software systems. His focus sector is insurance and banking. He loves to share his knowledge and experience at international conferences on a regularly basis.

title: From vibe coding to harness engineering: modernizing a regulated environment with AI
summary: AI-enabled migration of a banking mainframe to the cloud required a shift from “vibe coding” to “harness engineering.” The talk shows how to control AI-generated code in regulated environments through spec-driven development, evolutionary pipelines, and continuous validation, balancing agility, safety, and changing security rules.

speakers.name: Anyul Rivas
speakers.bio: Senior Solution Architect | Designing Scalable Systems & Leading Cross-Team Delivery at GFT | CTO Office | Software Crafter Barcelona leader | Barcelona JUG Leader

title: Snake in 10 Lines: Learning More by Coding Less
summary: A live-coding talk recreates Snake in 10 lines of JDK-only code, overcoming input and design challenges to distill the game’s essence. The project demonstrates how extreme conciseness fosters creativity, deeper understanding, and transferable problem-solving techniques.

speakers.name: Guus de Wit
speakers.bio: Guus is a Java/Kotlin engineer at adesso Netherlands. With a passion for puzzles and a background in science, he strives for elegant solutions to complex problems. In his spare time, he likes to over-optimize the simple tasks of today, to hopefully live a lazy life tomorrow.

title: Toxic Flows in MCP Servers and Skills: What Your Agent Blindly Trusts
summary: This talk introduces “toxic flows” in AI agent stacks: trust paths through MCP servers and Skills that can leak context, manipulate decisions, and trigger unintended actions. It shows how trust failures arise, parallels familiar software risks, and offers a framework for identifying boundaries and hardening agent integrations.

speakers.name: Brian Vermeer
speakers.bio: Staff Developer Advocate for Snyk, Java Champion, Oracle Ace Pro, and Software Engineer with over a decade of hands-on experience in creating and maintaining software. He is passionate about Java, (Pure) Functional Programming and Cybersecurity. Brian is a JUG leader for the Virtual JUG and the NLJUG. He also co-leads the DevSecCon community and is a community manager for Foojay. He is a regular international speaker on mostly Java-related conferences like JavaOne, Devnexus, Devoxx, Jfokus, JavaZone and many more. Besides all that, Brian is a military reserve for the Royal Netherlands Air Force and a Taekwondo Master / Teacher.

title: 223 Pull Requests in 11 Days: The Recipe for Building Real Software with AI Agents
summary: An AI-agent workflow enabled building an 83,000-line Spring Boot developer UI in 11 days instead of 6.5–8.5 months. The talk explains how to orchestrate multiple agents with specs, tests, and parallel overnight builds to achieve major productivity gains while delivering a new developer console.

speakers.name: Julien Dubois
speakers.bio:
Julien Dubois is a Java Champion and a Principal Manager at Microsoft. With his team of world-class developer advocates, Julien works directly with the engineering groups to improve how developers can leverage AI using Microsoft and GitHub solutions.

With over 25 years of experience in the Java ecosystem, Julien is best known as the creator of JHipster, an Open Source platform with 22,000+ GitHub stars that revolutionized how developers build Spring Boot applications. His recent work focuses on bringing enterprise-grade AI capabilities to Java through his contributions to LangChain4j and Spring AI.

Julien is a recognized thought leader in the Java community, having spoken at over 200 international conferences including Devoxx, Spring One, and Microsoft Build. He authored Spring par la pratique, the first French book on the Spring Framework, which became a bestseller. His presentations typically feature live-coding sessions and practical workshops that help developers immediately apply new technologies.

title: Java on Kubernetes Without Container Images: The WebAssembly Way
summary: The talk shows how KWasm-style runtime delegation can let Java apps run on Kubernetes without container images. It explains containerd internals, custom shims, node provisioners, and CRDs, then demonstrates Brewlet.sh, a new open-source project that deploys a Spring Boot JAR directly as an OCI artifact.

speakers.name: Bruno Borges
speakers.bio: Bruno Borges is a Principal Product Manager at GitHub with over 30 years of experience in Software Engineering, Product Management, Developer Relations, and Cloud & AI developer experience. Currently, he leads developer relations and product management programs for AI and GitHub Copilot at Microsoft, driving initiatives like the GitHub Copilot SDK for Java, and AI-assisted modernization workflows for enterprise developers. Bruno also continues to shape Microsoft's Java strategy, having led the public announcement of the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK and new tools like Azure Command Launcher for Java. Prior to his current focus on AI, he spent years building Microsoft Azure into a top destination for Java workloads, and before that served nearly six years at Oracle influencing developer relations strategy. A recognized Java Champion and top Java influencer, Bruno is a frequent conference speaker and open-source contributor with projects like Java Evolved, JairoSVG, JLib Inspector, ghx, and more. Visit github.com/brunoborges

title: Project Detroit: From Foreign Libraries to Foreign Language Runtimes
summary: Project Detroit uses Java’s Foreign Function & Memory API to embed native runtimes like V8 and CPython directly into Java applications. It replaces custom reimplementations like Nashorn with standard runtimes, exploring challenges such as garbage collection coordination and virtual thread pinning.

speakers.name: Maurizio Cimadamore
speakers.bio:
Maurizio Cimadamore is a compiler architect at Oracle. He is currently working on the language and runtime aspects of many foundational projects that will change the shape of the Java platform, such as Project Valhalla and Project Panama.
In the previous years, he has contributed to the design and implementation of several features of the Java programming language, such as diamond inference, lambda expressions and local variable type-inference. Maurizio holds a PhD in language design and implementation.

title: Reflect, Transform, Accelerate: Bringing GPU Computing to Java
summary: The talk presents HAT, a toolkit using Java Code Reflection to accelerate Java workloads on GPUs through reflection, transformation, and offloading to OpenCL or CUDA. It includes tensor-core and matrix-multiplication examples, plus performance profiling and tuning with NVIDIA Nsight Compute and Nsight Systems.

speakers.name: Juan Fumero
speakers.bio: Juan Fumero, PhD, is a Software Developer in Oracle’s Java Platform Group, specializing in JIT compilation, managed runtime systems, GPU programming, and heterogeneous computing. Previously a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester, he led the development of TornadoVM, a framework for accelerating Java applications on GPUs, FPGAs, and other hardware. He holds a PhD from the University of Edinburgh and has contributed to projects with Intel, ESA, CERN, and Oracle Labs.

title: How to Architect Green Software
summary: The session examines sustainability trade-offs in architecture decisions, balancing energy use and carbon footprint against maintainability, portability, availability, and performance. It offers practical techniques to reduce emissions and costs, and provides a catalog of trade-offs to apply in future projects.

speakers.name: Ioannis Kolaxis
speakers.bio:
Ioannis Kolaxis is a Director and a Senior Technology Architect at Accenture. He focuses on Green Software innovations, optimizing applications to have lower costs, reduced energy consumption and fewer carbon emissions. He is an inventor, speaker, and author of the Green Software book.
He was a kid in primary school when he first saw the green screen with the blinking cursor of an Amstrad CPC6128. This computer opened a new world to him, a world of continuous exploration and creation through programming.
Ioannis invented a novel way to work remotely and holds four patents for software solutions.
He frequently speaks at conferences such as GOTO Amsterdam 2022, Devoxx Ukraine 2021 and Oracle Code One 2019.
Visit his website to learn more: https://kolaxis.dev

title: When ORM Becomes OMG: Performance Pitfalls in JPA and Friends
summary: This talk examines common JPA performance pitfalls, from unexpected data loading and transaction issues to connection mismanagement. Using a sample app, it shows how libraries and tooling can reveal real-world ORM problems and help prevent slowdowns in Spring Data JPA applications.

speakers.name: Jos Roseboom
speakers.bio:
Jos gets a smile on his face when he makes other people happy by letting a computer do what they don’t like to do. He has been trying to do so professionally for the past 17 years.

In his spare time, Jos likes to play tennis. He is a trainer/coach for kids playing the typical Dutch sport korfball.

title: High-Performance Java-Native AI with CUDA and the Vector API
summary: This session shows how modern Java, using the Foreign Function & Memory API and Vector API, can run high-performance AI natively on CPUs and GPUs without JNI or Python. It includes Deep Netts CUDA integration, SIMD acceleration, and a fraud detection use case.

speakers.name: Zoran Sevarac
speakers.bio:
Zoran Sevarac is a seasoned software engineer, university professor of Artificial Intelligence, and passionate Java developer with more than two decades of experience in software engineering, AI research, and open-source innovation.
He is the creator of two pioneering AI development platforms built entirely in Java — Neuroph and Deep Netts — which made AI development more accessible to the Java community. His work bridges modern AI technologies with the reliability, performance, and scalability of the Java ecosystem.
A Duke’s Choice Award winner, Java Champion, and member of the JCP Executive Committee, Zoran has been instrumental in driving the evolution of AI support in Java. His mission is to simplify AI adoption, enable GPU acceleration through Project Panama and the Vector API, and bring high-performance, energy-efficient, and FinOps-friendly AI to enterprise systems.

title: Agents With Seatbelts: Practical Ways to Keep AI Code Gen Under Control
summary: This session shares best practices for MCP setups and AI agents in development workflows, focusing on quality, security, and avoiding unintended actions. It compares LLM code-generation stability and consistency, and addresses how to measure AI-driven improvement, helping teams build reliable, productive, and safe AI workflows.

speakers.name: Jonathan Vila López
speakers.bio:
International Speaker, JavaChampion, Cofounder of JBCNConf and DevBcn conferences in Barcelona, and AI4Devs conference in Amsterdam.
